title: Scalar compatibility of the resolution cohomology map
statement: For a scheme map h:X -> Y and an h-map phi:G -> h_*F, let D be any resolution data of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. For every p, r in O_Y(Y), and x in H^p(Y,G) of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], D.map(p)(r x) = h.appTop(r) D.map(p)(x).

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01F7, Equation 01F9 and Remark 01FB; Derived Categories 013P, 013S, 05TG for resolution comparisons

proof.text:
Proof: apply global sections to D.β and D.lambda. These are maps of modules over
O_Y(Y), so their maps on cycles and boundaries, and hence homology, are linear.
The inverse section comparison D.a.inv is restriction along the equality
h⁻¹(Y) = X by D.sections and respects the O_Y(Y)-action induced by h.appTop.
Consequently D.a.hom and the vertical homology map are O_Y(Y)-linear when
the X-side modules are viewed by restriction of scalars. Its inverse is also
O_Y(Y)-linear: apply the bijective vertical map to the desired scalar identity
and use linearity and injectivity. No inverse of h.appTop is required.
Finally the resolution isomorphisms and the
forgetful homology isomorphisms in D.map come from module morphisms and preserve
scalar multiplication. Composing these scalar identities gives the equation.
This is clause (1) of the parent's argument before bundling a linear map.

proof_origin.place: Parent basic-properties proof, clause (1), made precise for arbitrary resolution data

lean.statement: theorem ModuleCohomologyFMapData.map_smul {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {h : X ⟶ Y} {G : SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf} {F : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf} {φ : G ⟶ (pushforward h).obj F} (D : ModuleCohomologyFMapData h G F φ) (p : ℕ) (r : Y.ringCatSheaf.obj.obj (op (⊤ : Y.Opens))) (x : (Y.toRingedSpace.moduleCohomology p).obj G) : (D.map p).hom (r • x) = h.appTop.hom r • (show (X.toRingedSpace.moduleCohomology p).obj F from (D.map p).hom x)
